intent: A 2-3 minute product video for @instafill_ai aimed at REAL ESTATE AGENTS rather than at appraisers: the same Residential BPO form and the same synthetic Cantrell dataset the 9:14 walkthrough (neaCnEawvbk) used, re-recorded and re-cut under the angle 'how real estate agents automate paperwork with AI'. Plus one vertical short cut from it. Recorded SILENT -- the narration is a written ElevenLabs voice-over, not a live take.

form.breakdown: 455 text, 78 button, 1 choice -- measured with pypdf, which is where the '500+ fields' claim in the old video comes from
form.sections: I General Market Conditions, II Subject Marketability, III Competitive Closed Sales, IV Competitive Listings, and the adjustment grids

subject.what: the subject property: Pending at $151,800, 3 bed / 1 bath, 1,158 sqft, built 1928, condition 'Major Rehab Needed', tax assessed $241,200
subject.why_it_matters: context only, never a talking point -- see the angle note below. The price appears on screen because it is in the document; the voice-over does not mention it.

scope.what: Northline Restoration Co. rehabilitation budget for 946 Alderwick St -- demolition $10,500, roofing $9,500, HVAC $8,500, flooring $5,500, plus drywall, kitchen, plumbing, paint, cleanup

inputs._assets_are_committed: These nine PDFs live under assets/ and are IN GIT on purpose, against the convention that project content is gitignored. The precedent is the failure this project exists to avoid: projects/neaCnEawvbk kept only its manifests, its sources are gone, and the video it made cannot be rebuilt or re-cut today. 490 KB of synthetic data is a cheap price for a reproducible demo, and nothing here is real -- the addresses, MLS numbers, licences and phone numbers are invented.

recorder.screen: Cursorful (Chrome extension), exported at 1080p -- it auto-zooms to the cursor, which is the capability we were otherwise going to build. Reference of its output: sARFB1XnQKk (1:19), which is 1280x720 and demonstrates why 1080p has to be set explicitly.
recorder.camera: a phone on a stand, LANDSCAPE 1080p30, to the side of the laptop at ~45 degrees, 50-70cm, framing the hands and keyboard in the bottom two thirds with the laptop screen clipping in at the top, angled and unreadable. Never the face. One continuous take across all five screen takes, so sync-tracks.py can line the two up by itself.
recorder.why_two: the hand is the subject, not the screen -- the screen already exists sharp in the Cursorful recording, and filming it again only buys moire, reflections and an exposure that sacrifices the hands. Cutaways are 2-3s in two places: Submit, and the finished report.

controls.recording: projects/bpo-realtor/recording-plan.md -- the shot list the footage must come from; five takes, silent, no face

notes: Predecessor: neaCnEawvbk, 'How to fill out BPO forms with AI | Residential Broker Price Opinion', 9:14, with three vertical shorts. This project is NOT a re-cut of it -- the requirement is a new recording of the same form on the same data.

Angle settled 2026-09-23: NOT the valuation story. The data is synthetic, so leaning on $151,800-vs-$400k invites scrutiny of numbers we invented and points the viewer away from the product. The axis is input vs output -- eight documents the agent already has, 534 fields nobody types. 'The AI does the paperwork. Not you.'
No face, in any take. A written ElevenLabs voice-over over a filmed face is a lip-sync problem by construction. The phone IS used, but it points at the hands and the keyboard -- see inputs.recorder.

The phone is NOT used to re-shoot the demo in a mobile browser. That was considered and dropped: a 3-page 534-field PDF is unreadable on a phone, so a mobile take would make the vertical short worse, not better. Keep that idea for a video about a short, simple form.

Cursorful replaces the planned cursor-follow auto-zoom tool. Do not build it for this project; revisit only if a future recording cannot use the extension (e.g. File Explorer, which a Chrome extension cannot capture -- which is why take 2 shows the documents as browser tabs instead of as files in a folder).

Second-angle idea worth keeping: a PRINTED copy of the three-page form on the desk, a hand turning its pages -- '534 fields on screen, three sheets in a hand' is the argument in one image. Dropped for this shoot only because there is no printer. Blank A4 as a stand-in was refused: blank paper is not this form, and the difference reads as staging.
